utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber would like to inform the parties that pursuant to Rule 15 bis (A), today's hearing will take place in the absence of Judge Hoepfel. Judge Hoepfel is for urgent personal reasons unable to sit today, and the remaining Judges, that is Judge Stole and myself, concluded that it is in the interests of justice to continue the trial without Judge Hoepfel for the day. A few procedural issues. Let's try to keep it as short as possible. The parties will be aware that the testimony of Colonel John Crosland will resume next week, and the Chamber would like to ask the Defence whether they object to the admission of, first, the documents accompanying the transcripts from the Limaj case; and second, whether they object to the documents that the Prosecution tendered through the witness in its examination-in-chief. If there is an objection to the admission of any of documents, the Chamber would like to ask the Defence to specify the documents to which they object on the coming Monday. I think I earlier asked your attention for the advantages of the Chamber being aware prior to the continuation of the examination of Colonel Crosland. Then, finally, I will -- the Chamber makes a statement regarding two Prosecution's Rule 92 bis motions. Until, I think, one or two hours ago, the statement was longer than it is now, and that is due to the fact that today the Prosecution has filed a corrigendum to Prosecution's motion to admit written statements pursuant to Rule 92 bis, which only arrived, I think, this morning. Nevertheless, the Chamber makes a few comments on the Rule 92 bis motions filed by the Prosecution. On the 19th of February, 2007, the Prosecution filed a notice of a motion to admit written statements pursuant to Rule 92 bis. The motion contained the statements of and other material relating to 21 persons. The Defence responded on the 28th of February, on the 1st of March, and on the 2nd of March. On the 7th of May, 2007, the Prosecution filed a motion to admit statements of eight persons pursuant to Rule 92 bis. Seven of these persons were included in the original 19th of February filing. The motion does not explain how the material contained in the two filings compare, and in particular it does not explain what changes have been made to the original statements. The Chamber notes that some statements are identical while others have been amended to one degree or another, even if the motion is silent on these changes. One of the eight persons who is assigned Witness number 86 is indicated as a viva voce witness in the Prosecution's witness list of the 2nd of March, 2007. Although not clearly set out in the motion, the Chamber understands that the Prosecution now wishes to change this witness's status from viva voce witness to Rule 92 bis witness. The Prosecution should have clarified this new request in its 7th of May motion. The Chamber hereby brings this information to the Defence's attention in order to ensure that it will be properly and fully considered by them in their responses which are due the 21st of May, 2007. However, the Chamber also requests the Prosecution to be perfectly clear in future motions concerning Rule 92 bis how the material in those motions relate to previous motions, in particular the 19th of February filings. This concludes the Chamber's comments on the Prosecution's 92 bis motions. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: At two minutes to 2.00 this afternoon, we received an e-mail from Mr. Re concerning the scheduling of witnesses for next week. Without going into the details of it, it places the Defence in very real difficulty because there is currently of a high degree of uncertainty about who is coming and when they are coming, which makes planning on the current state of the information for cross-examination in practical terms impossible. Now, it may be that during the course of the afternoon, further information will become available, but could I invite Your Honours to request Mr. Re's attendance at ten minutes to 7.00 this afternoon so that a proper explanation can be given as to who it is we need to prepare to examine next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, may I -- one second, please. Yes, the Chamber has received a copy of this e-mail. Mr. Kearney, do you think Mr. Re would be available at ten minutes to 7.00?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I don't see why not, Your Honour. I will ask him at the first break, and I will have information for you at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There might perhaps even be a possibility to send him an e-mail so that if he has got anything else to do this afternoon, that he doesn't miss the request. The Chamber, of course, will read in more detail the e-mail and -- but at least the Chamber supports until now the presence of Mr. Re at ten minutes to 7.00. Anything else? Then could the witness be brought into the courtroom -- if at least, Mr. Kearney, you're ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am ready. I just wanted to bring one matter to the Court's attention. As the Court remembers, yesterday the Chambers found a discrepancy in the 92 ter statements. At the conclusion of proceedings yesterday, I spoke to colleagues on the Defence, specifically Messrs. Emmerson and Harvey. I did not have a chance to talk to Mr. Guy-Smith at the time. In any event, we spoke and counsel gave me their assent to the admission of the document if the Prosecution could submit to the Court that the two translations were accurate with each other. And I thank Mr. Emmerson and Mr. Harvey for that gracious gesture. Since yesterday, we've had an Albanian interpreter compare the two documents, and I'm assured that the only difference between them is the simple two words in that one paragraph the Court found of "lower Lluka" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: -- being in the English translation and not the Albanian. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that -- let me just cut this short. The discrepancy as such was not shocking. I would say also "return from lower Lluka" or -- because that appears in one of the other statements, and it's not of great relevance from where exactly he returned, I take it, at that moment. It was more shocking that there was a discrepancy. That was -- if that's just a translation issue or whether there's cutting and pasting is something of concern. Any further --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Simply, as a procedural issue in that regard, my understanding with this witness - and it may be with others, too - is that the 92 ter statement that was read to the witness and which he therefore attests to is the English version; in other words, it is read to him in English and then translated into Albanian orally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, of course, all the signatures under the other version are --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Unless I've got that wrong. In other words, it's important to know which statement it is that the witness has agreed is correct, insofar as there may be a discrepancy between them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And my understanding is that the witness read the Albanian version to himself, made corrections to the Albanian version and satisfied himself it was correct. Those changes were incorporated; he signed that document. That document was then translated based on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And not read again to him -- translated again in the other direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Correct. The English version was not read to him. If the Court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If they are the same, there seems to be not a major problem, but I'd like to -- not at this moment but to have this clarified for the future so that there's never -- that we always know, apart from -- I mean, it seems that witnesses are signing every statement in all languages just to make sure that it was before them, but then I'd like to know whether they read the statement they signed or whether the statement in a language they do not understand was translated back to them from that original, or both. Let's proceed --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think, if I may just say so, this inquiry began with Your Honour asking which is the authentic statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think the answer is the authentic statement is the Albanian statement, which the witness read and signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now we know that they are the same. Yesterday we spent quite some time on whether to use six or seven minutes in cross-examination, so let's get started with the witness. Could the witness be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Cekaj. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you gave yesterday at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Kearney will now continue his examination. Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, I want to just follow-up on one comment you had yesterday. You were talking about the -- the Serb artillery that you heard while you were still living in the village of Peje, and I want to ask you a few questions about that artillery, if I may. Mr. Cekaj, by my estimate, you spent over a decade in the Yugoslavian Army serving as a soldier in that army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As an officer, not as a soldier, not as a simple soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: My apologies, Mr. Cekaj. I'm sorry about that. I just want to ask you, based on your experience in the army, can you tell us anything more about the size of the guns you heard conducting this shelling and their possible range, if you know that size, please?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This could be artillery 120-millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And based on your own experience in the army, how far does a shell from a 120-millimetre artillery piece travel?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Although I did not belong to any artillery unit, I think that you can fire it up to 8 to 12 kilometres. It depends.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer, Mr. Cekaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I now, if I may, with the Court's permission, would like to move back into the document that we had on the screen yesterday. This is Exhibit P318.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, can you see that -- can you see that document clearly, Mr. Cekaj?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to put on my glasses, I can't without them, but I know the villages by heart.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, if it would be easier for the witness, I have a hard copy here. I'm not sure if it would be easier for him if we presented that to him during his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the way how you manage it, Mr. Kearney, but there's no objection against giving hard copies to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, is one of those easier for you to read than the other?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I can give an answer to you. I can see it [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, no markings until specifically requested, Mr. Cekaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, I'm just going to ask you, yesterday you said that - I'm quoting now: "This area in blue represented where the KLA soldiers could move at that time." Do you remember making that statement yesterday?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The KLA and the people who lived in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What do you mean by that, that they could -- the -- those people, the KLA and the civilians, could move freely within that area?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- I think that Mr. Kearney stretched the question a bit from what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness said something about moving, not about freely moving. That's not exactly the same under the circumstances, Mr. Kearney. Could you please explore that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, I thank my colleague for that suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Could you please explain what you meant, Mr. Cekaj, by saying that KLA soldiers and civilians could move within that area at the time you've indicated on the map?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Along the main road Peje-Decane-Gjakove. The villages that were close to the road were at risk, and the KLA soldiers were positioned there, in those villages, while in the internal parts they could carry other duties, secondary duties, or be with their families. So the situation was like that, that they also carried out other duties, family duties or other personal business.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And just --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. And just so we're clear, when you say the internal parts, what are you referring to, please?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The villages that were not directly vulnerable to the Serb attacks or that were under Serb attack from objects that were along this main road Peje-Decane-Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: For instance, you have a smaller blue circle drawn on that exhibit around your village of Irzniq. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And would you consider the village of Irzniq there one of the villages that was on the interior, as you -- or the internal part of the -- the zone that you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. My village connects all these villages that go -- when you go towards Decane, Prilep and other villages along the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, on top of the map, you mentioned yesterday that you wrote the words "April - June." In relation to this discussion we're having of the ability to move about within the internal parts of the zone, was it the same throughout that entire period or did it change, if you could tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, I'm sorry to have to correct Mr. Kearney, but the witness gave two different answers; that is to say, different as between themselves and different from what appears on the legend on the map. So dates become a matter of some importance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect to my colleague, that's exactly why I'm asking him this right now to explain further what he means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But perhaps then it would be good to specifically address the matter of what he said yesterday or -- but please proceed. Everyone is now alert.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, when you wrote the words "April - June" on the top of this exhibit, what did you mean?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked about April - June -- can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the Serb police left the village of Irzniq, this part, this area, was considered as a free area, and people could move freely in the area, while the KLA were in the villages, they were closer to the main road Peje-Decane-Gjakove, as I already mentioned. I can also mention these villages again. From Strellc, Isniq, Beleg, Carrabreg, Prilep, Rastavice, Baballoq. These were villages directly vulnerable, and they were attacked every day or shelled every day at certain intervals, while the other villages in the interior part --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, perhaps Mr. Kearney will put every specific question to you. There's no need to expand. We'd like to move as quickly as possible, and Mr. Kearney knows exactly what he would like to hear from you, so please focus on the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: During what period of time in 1998 was this a free area, as you've told us?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are speaking about the period until the second offensive. This was the question asked of me earlier, and I said that there were three offensives: The first one on the 25th of May; the second one that ended on the 11th and 12th of July; and the September offensive on the 8th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, when --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So until the second offensive, this area -- in this area people were able to move freely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, you just mentioned that the second offensive was on the 11th and 12th of July. I want to suggest to you, based on your earlier statement, did you mean to say the 11th and 12th of August --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, again I do apologise. But this witness has given two different statements about those dates in two different written forms, and so it's not, with respect, right or fair to put a passage from the witness statement without putting the corresponding dates that were put in the interview, which Your Honours have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have not checked yet. If they are the same, there is no need; if they're not the same, Mr. Kearney, you're invited to specifically refer to the portion of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: This is a passage which occurs, actually, in both statements, Your Honour, but for clarity I will refer to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The first large statement you gave last week, Mr. Cekaj, specifically to paragraph 47 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the objection still stands, and I think Mr. Kearney misunderstood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps could we do the following: Mr. Kearney, you read to the witness both versions, and you ask him which one is correct to the extent that it is not -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just be clear? I'm not referring to the two versions of the witness statement; I'm referring to the consolidated witness statement which Mr. Kearney is now referring to and the interview --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- which Your Honours have, transcript of interview at pages 100 and 107, where different dates are given in respect of this offensive from the ones that appear in the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I'm simply attempting at this time to refresh his memory in this regard --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if you want to refresh his memory and if there are sources all being the same witness who give different versions of the matter you would like to refresh his memory, then I think it would be fair that he would have the choice which of his -- I mean, it's not -- choosing one of his statements, if it's different from the others, I say that, of course, is a form of leading which I do understand Mr. Emmerson opposes against. And if you want to rely on the statement that -- the long statement, I think it was many, many pages, then would you please indicate where to find it because the Chamber --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I can assist Your Honours, it's pages 100 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me first see whether to find it, first of all, because we have not printed that out. Yes, is that the audiotaped 2005 interview?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly so, exactly so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. And then --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I've got it now on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The easiest place to find the relevant passage is on pages -- on page 107.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then, Mr. Kearney --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'd be happy to refer him to all three of his statements, Your Honour, if the Court would like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I haven't checked it yet, but if they -- if they're all quite different, then it would be fair to do so. If ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps we could have the witness take his headphones off for one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know. He greeted us in English, I don't know whether that helps. Do you speak any English, Mr. Cekaj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much anyhow for the "good afternoon" you gave to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take off your earphones for a second? Yes, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, in both the long transcript over the course of several pages from approximately page 100 to 107 or thereabouts that Mr. Emmerson's referred to, this witness describes the August offensive. In his statement of last week and the proofing notes or in the 92 ter statement this week, he also talked about August. It's the Prosecution's suggestion that when he said July just a moment ago, he was mistaken. I simply wanted to refresh his memory in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is that also the second? Because he referred to three -- let me just find it. I have to switch from one screen to another. He talked about three offensives or three -- and I think he situated the third in - let me just -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's 11.23, I think, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. He was talking about the 25th of May, the 11th and the 12th of July, and the September offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- the record, the position is this, that in the interview at page 107 and, indeed, at page 100, the August offensive is described as having occurred on the 7th and 8th of August; in the witness statement, at paragraph 47, on the 11th and 12th of August. And so if the witness's memory is going to be refreshed, then, in our submission, it must be refreshed by reference to the inconsistent dates that have been given.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, that sounds fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: -- I simply want to ask him what the month was of the second offensive, and he's got the month -- it's the Prosecution's contention that the month -- when he says July, he's mistaken, and I want to refresh his memory in that regard. I can do it with any of the -- the statements we're referring to here.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If I can simple add this, the reason this may be important is to understand how good this witness's grasp of dates in his evidence generally is, because it's a pattern that appears at various points in the statements that he's given. So rather than leading him through to suggest clarity, it will be in our submission, of greater assistance to the Trial Chamber to see how reliable this witness's memory is on dates to see the different various accounts that have been given --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's -- yes, at this moment -- yes, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: These are events that happened eight, nine years ago. I don't think it's out of the question to refresh his memory with the month that event happened nine years ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but isn't it true that -- let me just see -- yes. Mr. Cekaj -- oh, you've got your earphones on already. You said that the second offensive was on the 11th and the 12th of July. Are you certain about that you took the correct month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise for making a mistake. It's a momentary mistake I made. It's a lapse of memory. I meant to say August and, in fact, I said July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you meant --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's my mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The correct is 7, 8th August and 11th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said 7th, 8th, and 11th. Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney -- carefully listen to the question of Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, what happened after that August offensive? Did the KLA's ability to move within the zone that you're talking about change?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, the August offensive started on the 8th, 9th, 11th, and ended on the 12th. At that time, as I said earlier, the Serbian forces managed to penetrate into the inner parts of that area, up near Irzniq village from various directions, Prilep, Isniq, Rastavice, Irzniq, Baballoq, Gllogjan, up to the inside of Irzniq village and in other parts from Ratishe along the canal, and they came on the 12th of August with their units armed to the teeth, and set fire to the houses and looted and raided them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. That August of 1998 offensive by the Serbs, how many days did it last?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The August offensive lasted from the 8th to the 12th. It ended on the 12th, and they came back to the villages and we started to restructure the force in the villages. This went on until the 8th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: During --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 8th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: During that period of time, during the offensive, did the Serbs stay in the villages the entire period or did they enter and withdraw?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They entered, looted and raided, set fire to houses and went back to their bases to facilities where they were deployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: After the Serb forces withdrew from their August offensive, describe for us your ability to move around this area, this Dukagjini area that you've circled in blue, please?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was another sort of situation during which the houses had been burned and the population started to come back to their homes and the KLA member, wherever they could, return; that is, in the front part in their positions. And we started to restructure the ranks, the units, and the population gradually started to return, but it couldn't return to all the villages because they had been burned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'd like to move on, if we may, to your April meeting with Mr. Haradinaj. After that meeting, you indicated for us yesterday that you went back home to Peje. At some point after returning home, did you decide to join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I returned to Peje, it -- I went to my village in the second half of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You -- when you say your village, are you talking about Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you left Peje to come back to Irzniq, did you do it along the same general route through the villages you described for us during your April trip?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same route.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you encounter the same KLA check-points at that time that you had in April?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you arrived back in Irzniq in May, Mr. Cekaj, did you -- did you meet with the KLA village commander at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met the commander of the village staff and the deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The village commander was Mr. Maxhun Cekaj that you told us about yesterday. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, you know that we are under quite some time pressure. From your last seven or eight questions, I think five are in the 92 ter statement, such as questions whether he spent ten years in the army. That's all in the 92 ter statement, so please focus on something that's new and not ask the witness to repeat what he said yesterday and to ask him again. Of course, if you need to lead the witness in a certain direction, you can do that on the basis of the 92 ter statement say, Mid-May to the village, did you meet with so-and-so-and-so; if he then says yes, then you have saved four questions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for that suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you came back in May and you had this conversation with the village commander in Irzniq, you -- you mentioned in your 92 ter statement there was a command structure in place at that time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I want to ask you when that command structure was drawn-up and by whom, please?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That command structure was drawn as early as 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, the same what I just said is true for the last two questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And Your Honour, my apologies, but these are foundational to the next set of questions I'm going to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, please, next time say: When you discussed the command structure which, as you are told, was established in 1992, and then move on, because that's what the 92 ter statement says. And if you want to put that so that it's clear where we start from, you could do it also without asking the witness, because the witness has answered these questions in his 92 ter statement. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: This 1992 command structure that you're referring to, is that something that you actually saw, Mr. Cekaj? Is that a document that you actually examined at some point?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're talking about a document that was drawn by the members of the staff as early as 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Cekaj, do you have the question in mind? This command structure you're talking about was drawn-up in 1992, is this a document you actually had a chance to look -- look at and examine?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, paragraph 9: "They showed me the document that had been drawn-up in 1992."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I saw a plan, a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: My intent now, Your Honour, is to ask him about the contents of that plan, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next time, you say: The plan they showed you, I'd like to ask you some questions about the content of it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, can you please tell us about the contents of that plan that you were shown, the 1992 plan, if you could?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This plan showed the structure of the staff composed of ten members of this command. There was a battalion with two companies, platoons, and squads, and other parts involving the logistics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, I read from the 92 ter statement: "The command structure in Irzniq at that time was the following: Under the village command consisting of approximately ten people was a battalion consisting of two companies, within each companies were two platoons, and each platoon had three squads of seven or eight members." If you want to elicit additional testimony, apart from what's already in there, please specifically ask for it, because until now it's just -- just repetition of what's in the 92 ter statement, although you again and again tell me that you're now going to ask, it was just an introduction for your real questions, again and again the next questions are again exactly what we find in the 92 ter statement. 92 ter statements are there to save time. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, I want to move on now to a topic you did discuss briefly in your 92 ter statement, a meeting you attended in mid-May in Gllogjan when you came back to the village of Irzniq. Do you remember attending that meeting, first of all, Mr. Cekaj?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: After the main meeting was held, was there a smaller meeting of a lesser number of people than attended the main meeting?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the same night.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Who attended this small meeting in mid-May in Gllogjan when you came back to the village of Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I returned from Peje to Irzniq, the village commander and his deputy informed me that in the evening they had planned a meeting with all the commanders of the local village staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I want at this time to give notice of a desire to call-up 65 ter Exhibit 1337, Your Honour, while I ask some more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, during this -- this meeting that you're describing in mid-May in Gllogjan, who were the last remaining people to attend this meeting, if you could tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you want me to mention names, it was Ramush Haradinaj, myself, Skender Rexhahmetaj, Rrustem Tetaj, Gani Gjukaj, and other village commanders whose names I don't recall. I didn't know them. It was a considerable number of members.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: At that meeting, this smaller meeting at the end of the larger meeting, was there a staff created for the Dukagjin Zone?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And who were the members of that staff, if you can tell us, among those remaining?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time we functioned as a staff for the Dukagjini plateau, Ramush Haradinaj, myself, Skender Rexhahmetaj, Rrustem Tetaj, Gani Gjukaj, and some other members of the local staffs whose names I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: This staff that you're referring to for the Dukagjin Zone, how -- after that first meeting that you're talking about in May of 1998, how often did you meet?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes once a week or twice a week, and some other times more rarely, every two weeks. It depended on the circumstances on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Was there a particular place that these staff meetings were held?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We met in various places.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And please describe those places for us, if you could?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We met in Irzniq village, Gllogjan, Pozhare, Kodrali, Isniq, Lluke. These are the villages where we used to meet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, during this first staff meeting that you've told us about in May, were you given responsibility during that meeting regarding the KLA itself?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this meeting, I was given the responsibility to supervise some villages. Apart from my village, I had to supervise other villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And last week during your interview, did you draw a map of those villages that you were asked to supervise?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would like to call-up 65 ter 1337, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's already uploaded. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, these are -- or are these the villages that you were asked to supervise during that May meeting in Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was responsible for these villages, to supervise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Who asked you to supervise those villages?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agreed to do that. I was the one who proposed such a thing. We operated as a staff at that time. The situation was such that I took the initiative during that meeting, and the others agreed that we, as experienced leaders, undertake to assist in the organisation of daily life in these villages and the fire points, and other objectives we set ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, you're saying now that this was the decision to be responsible for these seven villages was your own idea. Is that my understanding?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were opinions, not decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: But, please, I would like to ask you again: This was your idea to take over the command of these seven villages?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We discussed many things, many issues, and then we came to the idea of someone supervising these villages and other villages that were given or assigned to my colleagues. This was an important question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, weren't you asked about -- asked this same question about how it was you came to command these seven villages during your interview and statement last week between the 9th and the 11th of May, 2007, here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a very hard night. There was shelling going on. The population was moving --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, the question was whether -- the same question that Mr. Kearney just asked you was put to you earlier, that is, a little bit over a week ago, during the interviews you had here in The Hague. Was the same question put to you, on whose initiative you got responsibility for the villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We discussed these issues, and then we came to the conclusion that we, as experienced leaders, should supervise some villages in addition to our own villages, in my case Irzniq. And other members proposed such a thing. So it came out first as a proposal, then I agreed to organise the daily life in these villages, having in mind the objectives we had set ourselves for the organisation, training, logistics, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't as if we were given strict orders; it was more in the form of a proposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And who made this proposal?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the meetings, these proposals came up spontaneously, I would say, but the meeting was chaired by Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: In your statement, Mr. Cekaj, don't you say that, this is in paragraph 21: "Ramush asked me if I could take responsibility for seven villages." Didn't you say that in your statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: But he didn't order me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did he -- did he ask you to take responsibility for those seven villages?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me, Can you take responsibility for these villages? He said to me, Can you do that? And I said, Yes, I agreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: During this period of time that you were given responsibility for these seven villages, what were Mr. Haradinaj's responsibilities in the Dukagjin area?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ramush Haradinaj at the time was just a member of the staff, of the Dukagjini Plain, and he was responsible for the village of Gllogjan and the area where these villages were: Baballoq, Dubrave, and Gramaqel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me -- excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might. In reading the transcript, the second question asked by Mr. Kearney on page 26, line 2: "Did he ask you to take responsibility for those seven villages?" is different from this gentleman's statement, which was read to him beforehand, which is if he could take responsibility. And I don't know whether or not the qualifying word of "could" is of importance or not, but I wanted to point it out because I think there is, in fact, here as a result of what we've heard thus far perhaps some subtlety with regard to how the decision ultimately occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And may I simply add this, and I don't want to take time over it, but again, from the interview record the relevant passage is on page 42 at the bottom, in which the witness explains the same area that he's now being asked about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can -- I think the point with this witness has been made. I can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is a good idea. Please do so. I take it, Mr. Guy-Smith, that the "could" and the -- is not something -- you have an opportunity in cross-examination if you want to revisit the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, I'd like to talk to you about Toger for a moment, if I may. What were his duties and responsibilities in the Dukagjin Zone at this time, in May of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, Toger was commander of the unit which in military terms is called the subversive sabotage unit, and the people called them the Black Eagles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How big was that unit?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never seen them lined up, but I think there were about 30 of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: If you know, when was that unit formed?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The black uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, when was that -- that unit formed, please?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was created at the beginning of April 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Where did they train, Mr. Cekaj?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they trained in some parts on the lands of the cooperative, close to Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: This is the cooperative on the east side of Gllogjan. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: North-east.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Where were they headquartered, please?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think at that time, it was in Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Where in Gllogjan were they headquartered?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said that I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'd like to call-up 65 ter Exhibit 1335 in advance at this time, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, after the period when they were headquartered in Gllogjan, this is the Toger's unit, did their headquarters move at some point?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: After Gllogjan, they moved and went to Irzniq.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, did they go to Irzniq at a time when Irzniq was in your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I had a different responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, but I want to ask you again: Was Irzniq in your general area of responsibility when the -- the unit we're talking about moved there?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Sir, I want to show you the photograph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before we continue, I think some numbers still have to be attributed. The map that we had yesterday on the screen was P318, that was giving the general area in which there was a relative free movement. Then the next one indicating the villages in the zone of responsibility of Mr. Cekaj, Mr. Registrar, that would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be marked for identification as P319.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and now the map we have on the screen at this moment would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be marked for identification as P320.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. For these three -- these two maps and this one photograph, any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Then they can be admitted into evidence including the marked photograph, P320. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, just to save time, please take a look at the photograph that is before you now. There are three circles drawn on that photograph, sir. Did you draw those circles?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And what were you describing with those three circles, please, if you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1 is the staff command in Irzniq that was in the beginning. After shelling that occurred between the dates of the 25th and the 30th of May, I went to the place which is circled and has the number 2. So number 1 and 2 represent the headquarters of the Irzniq village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, what was number 3?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 3 is the place where the anti-terrorist and sabotage unit stayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did that anti-terrorist and sabotage unit have a name?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Black Eagles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you ever go to this Black Eagles headquarters while you were operating in this general area in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, one second --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: One second. I do ask for specificity in question in response to answer given. The answer given that's where they stayed, there's not been an indication yet of anything other than that. It may well develop in that fashion, however it has not yet developed thus far in that way. So the last question asked by Mr. Kearney has not yet been answered by the witness in a fashion Mr. Kearney assumes facts in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I can rephrase the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you ever travel to this location, number 3? Did you ever enter the structure you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Why not, sir?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I was commander of 132 Brigade in Bardhaniq.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did Toger -- who did he report to? Who was in -- did he report to you, sir, as a superior?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not his superior, Toger's superior. I was commander of the 132 Brigade in Bardhaniq.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: But who did Toger report to then?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of our meetings, we discussed about the concerns we had, we analysed the situation on the ground, and as everybody else he reported and presented information about his unit. So he had this unit, a special unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: So he would come to staff meetings and make reports, but was there anybody who actually gave him orders?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We discussed together. There were no orders there. On the basis of the tasks given and decisions taken after the discussions, everybody went to their unit or area of responsibility to carry out those duties. This depended on the tasks each of us had and the situation, specific situation we found ourselves in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: During your time, Mr. Cekaj, as either area commander of the seven villages you talked about or brigade commander, did you ever become aware of any misconduct that was alleged to have been committed by Toger or Mr. Balaj?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Prosecutor, if you could ask the question more concretely. I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Certainly. Did anyone ever complain to you directly about the actions of Toger or, as we now know his name is, Mr. Balaj?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This has nothing to do with behaviours. If you're asking me about a case I mentioned, one morning in June a person called Besim, I already said that I am not sure about his surname, he came early one morning and informed me about a case. And I can describe the case like this, as follows: One day earlier Besim had met Toger by chance on the street, and he said that in the conversation with him, he had asked Besim whether he could help him do something -- do a job in a village. And according to him, he agreed to help. And they had agreed on a time where they would go, and Toger went at about 2200 hours. On the way when they were passing by the school at Prilep, they had seen the Serbian forces and there had been some exchange of fire. At that time, Toger had left towards Drenoc while Besim turned back towards his village, towards Rznic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The Serb forces had seen them and there were -- there was an exchange of fire, there were fire shots.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What did Besim tell you was the job that Toger wanted him to do?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was about a trench.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did Besim tell you why he was coming to you with this information?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said, Has anybody got the right to come and take me and ask me to work and do something? And I told him that I would talk to Toger about this, and from that time on he never took any other member of my village to do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Was Besim a KLA soldier?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Besim was a member who had gone to get a gun, so he had brought a gun, he had made his contribution. But because he was head of his household, he had to take care of his own family, he was the only one who could do that, he was not able to join the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you went and talked to Toger about this incident, what happened, please?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met Toger briefly on the street and I reproached him. I told him this should not happen. And he respected me, so he admitted he had made a mistake and nothing else of this kind happened after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you also -- or were you also made aware of shooting of a gentleman by the name of Adem Balaj in the general time-period of the end of July or the beginning of August 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Adem Hulaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I stand corrected. Thank you. Please tell us what information you received about that incident.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I was in Bardhaniq, but sometimes I went to visit my brothers at -- and in the evening, they told me about the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And what did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have it in the statement as well. My niece had been there, and she saw or heard the incident that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: During this incident, did Mr. Hulaj receive an injury?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that he was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How was he wounded?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not there, so I don't know he -- how he got wounded, I couldn't tell you, but he was shot in his leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you talk to your niece directly about this incident?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went there, she told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What did she tell you she saw exactly about this incident, please?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: She didn't see the incident because she was inside, but she had heard the shots and had gone outside after the thing had happened, and she had seen these persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Which persons did she tell you she saw?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, she didn't know them. I don't believe she knew them, but she saw Toger in uniform because it's very close where she was and it could be seen -- she could see that this was not something that he had done on purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Let me stop you there, Mr. Cekaj. You said that she told you that this was not something that he had done on purpose, that who had done on purpose?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that she told me, but, you know, when some -- somebody whispers, Why did I do this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Who did she tell you whispered, Why did I do this?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: She heard it because she was very close. Nobody told her.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Who did she tell you that she heard say this?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Toger.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: So, Mr. Cekaj, you received information from your niece that Toger may have been involved in a shooting incident with a person -- was, by the way, Mr. Hulaj a civilian or -- was Mr. Hulaj a civilian or was he in the military?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Hulaj was a civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And he was older. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, elderly man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: So, Mr. Cekaj, you received information that Toger potentially had shot an elderly civilian. Did you investigate that incident?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did anyone investigate that incident?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any other person?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes. Did anyone, for instance, within the KLA investigate that shooting?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of any other person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you know if Togeri was disciplined in any way for that shooting?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe yes, but I'm not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I also want to talk to you now about a visit you made to a woman in Ratis in June of 1998 to investigate a third complaint or another complaint. Do you understand -- or another incident, I should say. Do you remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you should not put the question this way because in June, I was responsible for those villages, Ratishe i Ulet and Ratishe i Eperme, and these villages were in the interior part, so they were safer. When I went there, the person responsible for the village told me that there is a family in a house in the outskirts of the village, and we went to visit them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Why did you go to visit that family?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said they live in a detached house. We discussed in the beginning if they had any problems, if they had enough food, and she said that the person who was responsible for the village was taking care of everything in her family. During the second visit --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, I'm sorry. I want to focus a question about this first visit for a moment. Why did you go to see this woman in Ratis?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason was that he told me this was a family that lived away from the village, and sometimes they had some concerns. But she didn't say anything about these concerns.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Were you shown a picture of this woman last week during your interview with the Prosecution? This is P16.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And did you recognise the woman in the picture?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the basis of the information, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Can I call-up, Your Honour, Exhibit P16, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think you will probably want to be in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: We should be -- that was my next thought, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, whilst that's being done, I wonder if Your Honour would be kind enough to excuse me for one moment. There's a matter I need to tend to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, You're excused.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Dixon will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you. And with the Court's concerns about time pressures in mind, I want to alert the Court that I intend to elicit information from two paragraphs contained in this witness's consolidated statement that he signed and initialed both in Albanian and in English last week between the dates of the 9th to the 11th of May of 2007, and those paragraphs are numbers 45 and 46.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, in the consolidated witness statement that you made in this case and signed last week, the larger of the two statements, at paragraph 8, you say this: "My brother Ali arranged a meeting between myself and Ramush. That meeting took place around 20 April 1998." And then a little further on at paragraph 11, you say: "When I went to the village to meet Ramush on 16 April 1998, I learned that the Irzniq KLA HQ had already been established." In other words, you give two different dates in the same statement a few lines apart. Now -- yes, in Irzniq. Now, can you help us at all, please, as to which of those dates is correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, during the interviews, there were also some misinterpretations made. I do not manipulate with dates. I said how -- in mid-April the date might be 20 or before 20. These are things which interpreters may confuse, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I see. You then return to Irzniq -- Irzniq in the second half of May. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Irzniq, not in the second half, but in -- in mid-May, sometime in mid-May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Is it correct that the day you returned to Irzniq was the same day as the day you went to the big meeting in Gllogjan where all the village leaders were there? Is it the same day?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the evening of the same day; that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, if I tell you that we've got invitations for that meeting that show that the meeting that you attended took place on the 26th of May, not in the middle of May, but on the 26th of May, if that's right, would that mean that that was the date you came back to Irzniq to take up your role in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date, nine years have passed. I never manipulated -- I just simply said mid-May. When I was invited to give an interview, I didn't mention any specific date. I simply said mid-April. It may say as you are putting it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Just a few moments ago, Mr. Cekaj, I put it to you that it was in the second half of May, and you corrected me and said it wasn't in the second half, it was in the middle of May. And what I'm now suggesting to you is that if you're right in saying that the day you came back to Irzniq was the day of the large meeting in Gllogjan, then that would have been the 26th of May; in other words, towards the end of the month.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And from that point onwards, you were the subzone commander for subzone 2, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: So immediately you arrived back in Irzniq, you took up the role as subzone commander of subzone 2?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And then within a day or two of that, there was a major Serb offensive at the end of May, was there not?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And you've described what took place in your witness statements at paragraphs 27 to 30, and it's also in the 92 ter statement. The next major milestone is the election of the Dukagjini Plain command, which took place on the 23rd of June; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: 23rd of June, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And the forces that entered Kosovo under the command of Tahir Zemaj, they first crossed the border at about that same time, didn't they, around about the 23rd/24th of June?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they came to Jasic, I don't remember the correct date, but I do know that they came to Isniq on the 30th. Maybe what you are saying is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: So they arrived in Isniq on the 30th --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to Isniq, Isniq.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And is it right that they had spent about a week in Jasic?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came to Isniq on the 30th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, and as far as --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As how long they stayed, this I am not sure about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Just to clarify one thing that's arisen earlier on. There are two villages called Jasic in the western part of Kosovo. The Jasic in which Tahir Zemaj's forces stopped, in other words the place where they first set up camp inside Kosovo, is that on the west side of the main road close to the Albanian border?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And you remained subzone commander for zone 2, for subzone 2, until the 12th of July, when you became commander of the 123rd Battalion, then -- then based in Bardhaniq and Zhabel. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was of 132nd --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I apologise. I apologise. 132nd. But that was a charge you took up on the 12th of April. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And does -- I'm sorry, 12th of July, I apologise, that's my mistake. 12th of July. And from that point onwards, from the 12th of July onwards, were you no longer in Irzniq at all?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And then I think in the major offensive that took place at the beginning of September, yourself and a number of other commanders retreated across the border to Albania on about the 8th of September?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were the units of the 134th Brigade. I had contact with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And is it right - just so that we're clear about the chronology - you then left Kosovo, towards Albania, crossed the border on about the 8th of September?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 8th, the 9th or the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, with that basic framework of dates, I now want to ask you some more detailed questions. First of all, had you personally been to either Irzniq or Gllogjan at any time between the 24th of March, when the Serb forces attacked the Haradinaj compound, and the 16th of April, when you met with Mr. Haradinaj in Irzniq? Had you been to either Gllogjan or Irzniq at any time between those two dates?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in Gllogjan, but in Irzniq, yes, I went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How many times had you been to Irzniq, roughly, during that period?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: About two or three times up to the day of the meeting with Ramush.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And had you spoken then to anybody who was trying to organise the village in Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, we did not discuss things thoroughly, not long discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Were you aware that there had been attacks on the police station at Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You don't remember one way or the other whether you knew that there had been attacks on the police station at Irzniq. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember when there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: In your witness statement, your consolidated witness statement, paragraph 8, you say: "I am not aware of any KLA attacks on the police station at Irzniq." Was that true when you wrote that, that you were not aware of any KLA attacks on the police station at Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in Irzniq at the time, I was not living there, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You were -- just told us a moment ago, you were visiting during this period?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the police withdrew. I don't think anybody attacked them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Well, I suggest there were fire-fights as between the police station at Irzniq and armed fighters in the village?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about the attack in Prilep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I see. You gave evidence yesterday that by the time you arrived back in Irzniq on the 16th of April, there were 120 soldiers in the village but 15 guns. Can you help us, please, in what sense were the 120 people there soldiers?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are misinterpretations because it depends on the question that is asked. In April, I don't think I knew about 120 soldiers that you mentioned. It is said like that in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: But at various times there have been about 120 to 170, but on the basis of that plan that we discussed that I mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You have recorded in your witness statement, and you were asked some questions about it a little earlier, on the fact that someone showed you a document that had been drawn-up in 1992 setting out battalions. Is that the truth, Mr. Cekaj, a document drawn-up in 1992? You saw that, did you?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And what -- did it have names of recruits in it?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw that very briefly because that was not valid at the time. This was something that had been drawn-up in 1992 on the basis of the situation in the years 1991/1992, and it said there that there was this staff with ten people --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and they had thought about the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had made evaluations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, are you suggesting that the battalions that are recorded as existing in that 1992 document are battalions of the KLA? Is that your suggestion?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only on paper, and that was kept secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The KLA didn't exist in 1992, Mr. Cekaj, did it?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had drawn-up that plan, very confidential plan, and up to that day they had never shown it to anyone openly, because of security reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And who had drawn that plan up, Mr. Cekaj?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the village, I mentioned him earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And he told you he drew it up in 1992, did he?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'm just going to read to you --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: And his deputy as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'm just going to read you something that you told us yesterday this is transcript 4390, line 4, when you were being asked questions about what happened after the 24th of March. You said this: "At that time the KLA had just started to organise in the villages that were under attack, after the event or the incident of the 24th in Gllogjan, so they organised to defend their villages in the event of a Serb attack so that the Serbs would not penetrate into the villages." That, that was the testimony you gave yesterday. Can I be clear, are you suggesting that there had been a designed organisation in Irzniq since 1992?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was just a plan that the commander and the deputy commander had drawn-up. They had kept it secret. That plan was not valid at the time we're speaking about, when the KLA came out openly in the villages that I mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The first time you'd ever heard of the KLA was at the end of November 1997, isn't that right, when they emerged at a funeral in Laushe. Is that the first time you had ever heard --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, let's try to understand what the witness wants to tell us. Mr. Cekaj, you talked about a plan, as you said, on paper. You told us that it was made in 1992. Could you tell us: Was that plan already KLA plan or just something like how to defend the village if need be or was it specifically called KLA or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Your Honour, a plan described the command of a battalion. A battalion had been formed. The organisational structure of this battalion was there. About 200 people were mentioned there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll stop you there. I'm not interested in the details of the plan. What I would like to know is: Was the plan about: We need some structure for the defence of our village if need be; or was it: This is a KLA plan. Was it rather general or was it already focusing --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
