utterances.text: [Interpretation] The KLA was not mentioned in the plan, of course. That was to defend the village in the event of an attack. It was a very difficult time. Yugoslavia was breaking up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Attacked by whomever, is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that could happen, yes. That was the essence of the plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said in answer to questions from Mr. Kearney that by the time you met Mr. Haradinaj in Irzniq on the 16th of April, the Serb police station had already been evacuated, there were no Serb police officers in the police station, and --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, yes, but on the basis of what I heard when I talked to some people. And on the 16th of April, the KLA came out openly in the village of Irzniq.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I see. You even gave us a specific date yesterday, transcript 4403, line 18, you gave us the 14th or 15th of April as the date when the Serb police left Irzniq. Where did you get that date from?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the information I got from my co-villagers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I want to suggest that you're wrong about that also and that the Serb police were still in control of Irzniq police station when you met Mr. Haradinaj, and that it remained fully manned until the 21st of April, when the police were first evacuated.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be like that. You could be right, but this is -- what I said is on the basis of the information I had at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, may I draw your attention where you said the witness specifically gave the 14th or the 15th --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that he said it must have been, which sounds very much as a conclusion related to other dates, which you just -- so therefore, to say that that's -- perhaps the calculation is right, the date is wrong, that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's always a possibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record, without drawing it -- taking time to put it up onto the screen, 65 ter, Exhibit 388, is a Pristina Corps command document which records the evacuation of Irzniq police station on the 21st of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, I want to suggest to you that even after Irzniq police station had been evacuated, there were still police patrols visiting the police station. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I don't know about that. I was living in Peje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You gave evidence yesterday that while you were living in Peje, you could hear shelling of Smolice, Baballoq, and Dubrava from the end of March onwards. And you described these as concentrated attacks, intensive attacks with a certain intensity. This is transcript 4387, line 9. Again I suggest that you are wrong about that, that there was no substantial shelling taking place at all between the 24th of March and the 21st of April, when Serb forces stationed at Suka Baballoq first began shelling the village of Baballoq.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I object to the term "substantial." That's inherently vague.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it means, Mr. Kearney, that's at least how I understand it - I take it that Mr. Cekaj also understands it that way - that it is suggested to you that there was no shelling, perhaps apart from an incidental shot fired, but there was no substantial shelling taking place at all between the 24th of March and the 21st of April. That's what Mr. Emmerson puts to you. Would you agree or do you not agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was shelling on Smolice and the Suka that was mentioned. There was fighting as well, as I already said earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is: When that took place? Was it before the 21st of April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was before the 21st of April in Smolice; that's what I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Just to complete the suggestion that I'm putting to you that the first shelling began on the 21st of April and that after that it was more or less continuous, but that there had been no shells, no shelling, prior to Orthodox Easter. That's the suggestion I'm putting to you.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was shelling in Smolice because the KLA was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: But not in Dubrava and not in Baballoq. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Smolice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I see. So we qualify the evidence you gave yesterday, because yesterday you gave evidence that there was shelling in Smolice, Baballoq, and Dubrava from the end of March.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Baballoq and Suka e Hereqit, those two are very close to each other, and there was shelling. That's what I think, that's what I believe. 64-millimetre, 82-millimetre, mine-launchers, mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And do you think you could be mistaken by a month about the dates?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I may be mistaken. I'm not very good with dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Let me move then on to where the Serbs were stationed when the shelling began in earnest. I'm going to suggest to you that once the shelling began in earnest on the 21st of April and from that time onwards, there were Serb artillery positions on three main hills in that area: Suka Baballoq, Suka Bitesh --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: -- and Suka Cermjan. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, and also the shooting range close to Peje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. And at least perhaps we can agree on this much, that once the shelling began it was more or less a daily occurrence?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you call-up, please, P318, P318?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: That is the map that you were giving evidence about earlier on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When we are waiting for that, could I ask the witness to take off his earphones for a second. Yes. Yes. Mr. Emmerson, yesterday the witness testified about hearing shelling from Pec and at a distance of 12, 13, 14 kilometres, not knowing exactly what was shelled, just by hearing, and then he shifted a bit by he said at what he saw later as damage. Therefore, I wonder, unless this could be clearly established, that this information where the witness now again said a couple of times "That's, I believe, what happened," that either we need a proper basis for it, both for establishing what he said he had heard but also for then perhaps denying or changing or -- that's just an observation --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If Your Honour hears --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just wanted to let you know that we carefully listened to what was said yesterday --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and the solidity of the basis of knowledge at such a distance by hearing is not such that I expect that the Judges would immediately, without giving it any further thought, agree on the reliability of such observations.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so -- and Your Honour sees that my case is that there was no shelling taking place during that period, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, there was or not but to say exactly here and there and from that position, that's -- that's, of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, if Your Honour's asking about those matters, then I need to explore the basis for the evidence that was just given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you also could understand that the basis given yesterday was not a very solid --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The less solid --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Totally understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it needs less to be contradicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Totally understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: By the time -- I'm sorry. Mr. Cekaj, by the time you got back to Irzniq at the end of May, was the shelling still continuing?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: So from that point onwards when you were based in Irzniq from the 26th of May onwards, were you then able to see Serb artillery positions on the three hills that you've just identified?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Taking into account the geographical position of these villages, the Serb positions were in -- in dominating areas, in higher-elevated areas where they were concentrated. And they attacked every day at certain intervals, they shelled every day, but there were also attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And -- well, let me take that last answer in two stages. First of all, when the shells and missiles were being fired, can you see from the trajectory of the shell or missile where it is being fired from?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. And you said in your last answer just a moment ago: "They shelled every day, but there were also attacks ...?" What do you mean by that, the attacks that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: From that date onwards, they attempted to attack Carrabreg, Prilep, Rastavice, Baballoq, and other villages close to the main road. These were everyday attempts from that day onwards. So they attempted intensively to enter the area close to the Carrabreg school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: As far as you understood it, was it the military strategy of the Serb forces to try to force their way in to the territory that you have marked here and the strategy of the KLA to try to keep them out?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was imposed on them, the geographical position dictated this kind of defence. It was not by chance that they chose to attack Baballoq and Gllogjan. They did this intentionally because the Serb forces wanted to enter that area and to penetrate into the villages in the interior parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you know whether the Serb forces that were stationed on those three hills, Suka Baballoq, Suka Bitesh, and Suka Cermjan, do you know whether they were mounting operations on the ground from those positions, as well?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Were there Serb forces on the ground as well as on the hills?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Vague as to time. When are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the hill and the dominant facilities, they put the artillery there, while in the other parts, the infantry were trying to penetrate with motorised vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'm going to deal with time in just a moment. Looking at this map that you've marked and the blue line that you've marked, Suka Bitesh and Suka Cermjan are inside the area you've marked, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Can I try with you, please, to understand what it is you're trying to depict in this map in terms of time. Just bear with me for a moment. Earlier today in answer to Mr. Kearney, this is transcript 1120 -- 11, line 23, you said that the area which was bounded by the blue lines was intended to convey an area of ability of the KLA to move up until the time of what you described as the second offensive, which you told us took place between the 7th and the 12th of August. That was the evidence you gave to Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I see. Could we just look at what is written at the top of the map there again for a moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I believe my colleague misstated this witness's earlier answer, Your Honour. He was -- he's referred to the 8th of August not the 7th of August as the inception date.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In fact, he's given two different answers in relation to that question to Mr. Kearney in his evidence this morning -- earlier today. It perhaps doesn't matter for these purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It isn't crucial for these purposes. That's my recollection as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, you now say that it's intended to describe a situation up until the early part of August. What you've written at the top of the map is April to June. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not clear about your question. Can you please be more explicit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The dates you've written on the top of the map say April to June 1998, don't they?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you -- I was asked about April and June, whether -- where the forces were and could they move freely, I mean the KLA and the population, it was in the interior part, whereas the Serbian forces were outside the main road. In the interior part, they could move during this period of April, May, June, up to the offensive first or the second offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Well, the first or the second offensive, Mr. Cekaj, it's rather important to the Trial Chamber to understand the dates that you're referring to. In the witness statement you made in this case, the consolidated witness statement, at paragraph 9, you said about this map, you said: "After the Serbs withdrew from the Irzniq police station in April, the territory around Irzniq was controlled by the KLA. I have drawn on a map the area that was controlled by the KLA and was considered free territory from this point in time until the Serb offensive at the very end of May that I describe later in this statement." In other words, when you made your statement to the Prosecution last week, you said this map was intended to refer to the position between the withdrawal of the police from Irzniq police station, which we know was the 21st of April, until the Serb offensive, which we know took place on about the 28th of May? But this afternoon, you said it was intended to cover the period up to the beginning of August. The map itself says April to June, and yesterday you said it's meant to relate to May and April at one point, transcript 4404, line 5, and then a little later you said it's not meant to refer to April but to the period after the 15th of May, 4405, line 15.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered to the question asked of me, and the offensive you mentioned is correct. I said this even earlier, it happened in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: So is your statement right, then, at paragraph 9 where it says that what you meant by this map was to describe the position as it stood until the Serb offensive at the end of May? Is that what you really meant by this map?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this time, April, May, June, apart from the first offensive, after which the Serbian forces withdrew, as you said, on the 28th of May, the dates may be wrong, may be incorrect sometimes. But this happened in May, the first offensive. That's why I described them as three offensives and not as two.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the attack, the Serbian forces withdrew.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I understand that, Mr. Cekaj, I understand that, Mr. Cekaj. What I'm putting to you is that in the statement you made, you said that this map was intended to describe the situation from the time the police left Irzniq police station until the Serb offensive at the end of May. Is that -- is what you said in your witness statement the truth? Is that what you meant to convey by this map?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened even after that. The dates of the offensives that were launched in August and September.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You, of course, weren't there until the 26th of May, until just before the offensive that we're talking about, were you?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where do you think I was?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You were in Pec, Mr. Cekaj, until the 26th of May.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This offensive which I mentioned may have occurred between that date and the 30th of May --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- it may be so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first offensive, the Serbian forces, which were estimated to be about 1.000 forces, attacked in the direction of Peje along the Peje-Decane-Gjakove road and another part, Raushiq, and in the villages of Barani valley. This is the offensive that -- during which during the day the forces withdrew.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, I'll move on. I want to ask you now some questions about the meeting that you attended on the day you returned; in other words, the meeting that took place in Gllogjan on the 26th of May, as I've explained to you where the records show the invitation was for the 26th of May. You've, first of all, described this in your consolidated witness statement, only parts of which --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For Your Honours' note are in the 92 ter statement. And I'm looking now at the consolidated witness statement, paragraphs 20, 22, 23 primarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: First of all, in the witness statement that you made last week, paragraph 20, you said that the meeting of the 26th of May was of villages in the Dukagjini area, all of which had a KLA staff. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the local staffs of the villages took part in it, at least those who could make it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I see. And I think it's right that there was a group that couldn't come, that was those who were on the western side of the road, of the main Peje to Gjakove road, weren't able to be there is what you said in your witness statement?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, yes, it was the beginning for me. I didn't know everyone, but I think, yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, you say in your witness statement that these village KLA staffs: "Had been independently organised and were not connected with Gllogjan." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- they were self-organised, but of course they cooperated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, but they were not at that point, prior to the 26th of May, they were not connected with Gllogjan. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe they met, but they didn't have any commanding relationship.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You say that Ramush -- this is a quotation from your statement, paragraph 20: "Ramush opened the meeting but not as a commander of the area. If he was a commander at that time, he was a village commander." Is that an accurate reflection of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You then go on to say that: "From that moment on, the four of us," this is paragraph 22, I'm sorry. "From that moment on, the four of us, Rrustem Tetaj, Skender Rexhahmetaj, Ramush, and myself worked as a team as part of the Dukagjini operative staff, but there was no overall commander." Is that your recollection?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were also other members in that staff, but I don't remember who they were. But this is a fact. It operated as a staff but without any commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: That may be so organisationally, but it is right, isn't it, to say that at least from the 26th of May onwards, even if you were all of equal status technically, Ramush Haradinaj was the man who was trying to organise in the area?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is very correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: He may not have been formally your commander, but he was - perhaps it's fair to say - the first among equals. Is that a fair expression?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ramush Haradinaj was someone who was very important and enjoyed great respect, and what you said is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Paragraph 23, you say this, and perhaps maybe this is an encapsulation of the point you're trying to make, so I'll just read to you what you say at paragraph 23: "I wasn't reporting to Ramush as his subordinate because I didn't consider him my commander." Is that really how you understood it?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct. I don't think that's correct. Can you show me where I said this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, it's paragraph 23 of your witness statement. I'll just read it to you again to make sure the translation's come clearly through to you. You say: "I wasn't reporting to Ramush as his subordinate because I didn't consider him my commander. We had the same positions at the time and operated as a staff." That's what your statement says. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very incomprehensible for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It cannot be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you want to just explain to us in your own words what it is you mean, then?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It was a joint proposal that we operate and work as a staff, but I think that this is a misinterpretation of my words; namely, that I have said that I don't accept and recognise him as a my commander. This is something which I don't agree with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I see. Well, can you just be clear, did you see him as your commander after the 26th of May or didn't you? Was he in command of you or were you equals?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the sense that I understand it, he enjoyed great -- he had my -- he had all my respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: But from the meeting we had, because of the situation, we acted as we did. But with respect to my consideration of him, I held him in high respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. I wasn't suggesting anything else. I wasn't suggesting that you don't hold him or didn't hold him in high respect. I want to put one further passage to you from that same paragraph and ask you, please, to confirm if it's correct: "Ramush travelled frequently around the area as well. He was particularly focused on the area around Carrabreg because it was in a difficult situation. I probably saw Ramush approximately once or twice a week during this time. We also occasionally communicated by courier." Can I ask you to confirm that that is a correct statement of your evidence, please?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct, but you cannot sum up Ramush's activity in just two words because his contribution was very specific one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes. No, I understand that but the point I'm trying to clarify with you, Mr. Cekaj, is that Ramush was always on the move during this period of time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, Ramush Haradinaj was a very energetic person. He was always on the move and followed from close up the fighting in the role of commander that he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: He would be on the front line where the fighting was taking place. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: In fact, he was injured, wasn't he, in the end-of-May offensive?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was injured in the May offensive at the Carrabreg school, and it's a fact for all to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And just to be clear about that, the battle at Carrabreg in which Ramush Haradinaj was injured at the school took place on the 28th of May. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that period from the 25th to the 28th, 30th I think, there were fightings every day on the part -- or attempts on the part of the Serbian forces to penetrate that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You yourself, I think, after the 26th of May, you yourself travelled around your own area quite a lot. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Between the 26th of May, when you were appointed subzone commander, and the 12th of July, when you stopped being subzone commander in Irzniq, you were visiting the villages in your subzone on a daily basis. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, the canal that leads down to Lake Radoniq flows right through Irzniq, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Right by the Serb police station there. Is that right? Do I have the geography correct? Is it very close to the Serb police station in Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I want to suggest to you quite specifically that the territory around the canal was disputed territory, a sort of no man's land for much of the time between your arrival on the 26th of May and your departure on the 12th of July. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object as to vague. What part of the canal are we talking about here? That's a very important issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Um --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The full length of the canal, the territory along the length of the canal between Irzniq and Lake Radoniq was an area where Serb forces were operating on the ground and shooting at people who they saw?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Again, I'm going to ask that we specify an exact time-period on this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think, as a matter of fact, that Mr. Emmerson did so. He said between the 26th of May and your departure on the 12th of July, that -- unless there is any -- that is a quite specific time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: So, Mr. Cekaj, do you understand the question I'm putting to you? I'm suggesting to you that between the 26th of May when you arrived and the 12th of July when you left, there were Serb forces, including paramilitaries, operating from time to time in the territory along the canal?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information about that. It was impossible for the Serbian forces to enter there at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you go there yourself, Mr. Cekaj?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have any contacts. I didn't go there. I went up to Ratishe and returned. I didn't go to that zone. In Ratishe, too, I went very rarely because I didn't have to, but in other villages I went more often.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When the Serb forces shelled and moved in to Gllogjan, how did they cut off the line of retreat for people to retreat towards Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Again, I'm going to ask during this series of questions that we specify exact time-periods, exact offensives, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There it would make sense to have a time --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: During the time that you were there --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a more concrete question. During the second or the first offensive, after the offensive of the 28th of May, the offensive was on the 8th, 9th, 12th. On the 8th, they started shelling, tried to enter the area from Baballoq; then they penetrated in Gllogjan, Shaptej. On the 11th, the Serbian forces entered, and, as I explained earlier, they came up to Irzniq village, went back -- withdrew, in fact. And on the next day, they attempted again and came from all directions. A member of the KLA in the vicinity of the canal, in the part along the road that goes to Ratishe was killed by the Serbian forces. It was possible for the Serbian forces to enter that far, until the inside of the village, but they withdrew after they accomplished their mission, after they looted and raided and set houses on fire and destroyed, inflicted material damage, they withdrew. Maybe they went up to the canal as well in the course of all these operations, because the KLA soldier was killed exactly there on that day, and his name is known and people know who he was. So when they came from that site, the infantry, the motorised vehicles could go up to that spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, it's not entirely clear to me what we are now talking about. Your initial question was about the 26th of May until, well, early July, and now it seems that the witness describes what happened in August, at least that's what I take it from "on the 8th, they started shelling," he apparently is talking about the second offensive. So therefore, I'm missing the link between your initial question --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I see the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and at the same time, I'd like to perhaps ask the witness: Mr. Cekaj, Mr. Emmerson asked you a question about the period when you arrived, late May until early July when you left, about whether there were any troops on the ground near the canal. And then you said, Well, I never went there. And a moment later, you said, Well, I went to Ratishe. Now, do I understand well that if you go from Irzniq to Ratishe, that you have to cross the canal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we must divide the time when I went to Ratishe. Ratishe was far, I went there very rarely. At that time, the canal between Irzniq village and the neighbourhood which belongs to Irzniq called Dodaj, this is where the canal passes, goes to Radonjic Lake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me ask you now. You said -- we have to make a distinction. When -- did you go between your arrival in late May and leaving in early July, did you in that period go to Ratishe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I went there two or three times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you came from Irzniq.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From my village, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So then from what I understand for the map -- from the map - but please correct me when I'm wrong - that you go into the area where the canal is, the canal that leads to Lake Radonjic; yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, did you, when you went these two or three times from Irzniq to Ratishe, where you had to go through the canal area where you had to cross the canal area, did you ever observe any Serb ground troops in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, there weren't any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I'm looking at the clock. We'll have a break now, anyhow. May I ask Madam Usher to -- we'll have a break, Mr. Cekaj. Madam Usher will escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time would you still need, Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think I can conclude in 25 minutes. I've discussed the matter with Mr. Guy-Smith, and I think between the two of us we're confident that leaving Mr. Harvey his short period of time, we'll conclude today. Obviously, the shorter the break can be the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time, did you also discuss the need for re-examination with Mr. Kearney?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I rather thought he'd had his limit so far by taking more time than he'd been allocated, but I'm in Your Honour's hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask just for a very small amount of remaining liberties, just another five to ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but adding up all these five to ten minutes, you would, you said, Mr. Emmerson, you'd need another 25 minutes. That brings us to at least 6.30, and then Mr. Guy-Smith -- of course you initially asked for 50 minutes, you've got 50 minutes, and then that brings us to 7.20 and then another ten minutes for you brings us to 7.30. Now, I understand that you could limit yourself to -- Mr. Guy-Smith, I'm confident where others sometimes speak too quick you even could speak a bit quicker now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, will do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Emmerson, if you would try to finish in 20 minutes, and if Mr. Guy-Smith, if you would be able to finish then in -- also in 25 minutes instead of the 30 you had in mind, then five minutes for you, Mr. Kearney. So we resume at five minutes past 6.00 up till 6.25 for Mr. Emmerson up till -- yes, Mr. Harvey, the remainder of the time, the six minutes, are yours, that's -- but you were so precise that we don't have to reduce them. Then until ten minutes to 7.00 for you, Mr. Guy-Smith. Then six minutes -- if you can do it in five, Mr. Harvey, would be even better. And then the Chamber -- at least I would have one question, Mr. Kearney will be left with very little time. We adjourn until five minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, after the --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I have a request to make, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to private session because I have a question to ask?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do not know what the question will be, but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- out of an abundance of caution, we'll move to private session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a very brief question.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. We're back in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, you told a littler earlier on that after the 12th of July, you were no longer based in Irzniq. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Irzniq, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You were thereafter based in Zhabel. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the school in Zhabel, in Jablanica, as a matter of fact. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: From the 12th of July onwards?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, until the 21st of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Where were you during the Serb offensive in the first half of August?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the Serb offensive, the first part of the offensive, I was in the area, in Bardhaniq, Zhabel, Grgoc, until that day. During the offensive, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Were you in Gllogjan or Irzniq when the Serb forces took control of those two villages in the August offensive?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 11th, when the offensive occurred, I was in Irzniq. Usually when I returned from Bardhaniq, I went and visited them at their positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You say when the Serb offensive occurred on the 11th. Now, you gave evidence a little earlier on that it started -- first of all, you said on the 7th and went on till the 12th, and then you said on the 8th and went on till the 12th. Now, Mr. Cekaj, were you, in fact, there during the Serb offensive?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is unclear to me. I don't understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, you described the offence as to have taken place during several days, starting the 7th or the 8th. Have you been in Irzniq all that time or just, as you said, on the 11th, or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only on the 11th, and I was there quite by chance. As a matter of fact, I was in Bardhaniq, but on the 7th and the 8th the shelling started, at least as far as I remember. Jablanica was attacked on the 8th by the -- it was attacked by the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- Mr. Cekaj, please carefully listen to the next question of Mr. Emmerson. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I just want to be very clear whether you were in Irzniq or Gllogjan when the Serb forces came into those villages and took control of them. When the ground forces entered those villages, were you there or not?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the morning, but in the hours of the afternoon we withdrew to Kodrali, Pozhare, and other villages in the interior part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You see, we've heard evidence just a couple of days ago from an international monitor who was in Irzniq and Gllogjan on the 11th of August and who has said that at the time that he was there, Serb forces were approaching but had not yet taken control, either of Irzniq or of Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 11th in the evening, they entered Irzniq -- Irzniq and then withdrew, but the next day in the morning hours they undertook an offensive again in the same directions. They entered Gllogjan, the area that I mentioned earlier, so the part of the canal shore, and entered Irzniq and other villages, and the villages were looted and set on fire. And that is very true. But then they still withdrew again because the population had left the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And were you there when they entered and were looting?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could not see them, but the next day we saw that the villages had been looted and burnt, and the whole international community could see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Were you --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Does it follow from the answer you've just given that you were not there when the Serb forces entered those villages, you personally were not there?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean I was not there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: It's a simple enough question, Mr. Cekaj. Were you in either of those villages when the Serb forces entered the villages on foot and when --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We withdrew.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: So did you see them approaching? Did you see them approaching, yourself?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They attacked until the afternoon hours, and the KLA forces withdrew because they could not resist the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And then they came back again, is that what you're saying, a second day?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the late hours of the evening, the Serb forces withdrew, and the next day they started the attack again on this village -- on these villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I want to ask you now some questions, please, about where the Black Eagles unit was located during the time that you were the subzone commander, that month or so between the 26th of May and the 12th of July. Just bear with me for a moment. You've said in your interview - and I think as well in your witness statement but certainly in your interview - that for a time the Black Eagles were stationed in Voksh. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Counsel, I'm sorry, what portion of his statement are you referring to now?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm looking at certainly page 116 of the interview, if that assists.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Is it right, Mr. Cekaj, that the Black Eagles were for a time located and stationed in Voksh?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I believe -- I believe that misstates the transcript, Your Honour. It says -- I have a different reading of page 116. Perhaps we could read the exact passage to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please put to the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You were asked in your interview about your knowledge of the Black Eagles. And you said: "In my region where I was, they were never present." Then you said: "They were never seen where I was operating." And then you were asked: "Were they a unit who could operate in all Dukagjin?" And you said: "As I said before, they were, ah, in movement, they were moving. "I have seen them passing through the village. For a while they were in Voksh." Do you remember a period of time when the Black Eagles were in Voksh?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the following developments, the Serb forces were attempting continuously to block the supply route from Albania, and this unit, as a subversive unit, had the task to go to these interior parts and secure the canal where they always went to get weapons and to carry the wounded. That was the mission of the unit at the time in Sllup, Voksh --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, try to focus on the question. You said they -- "For a while, they were in Voksh." Was there an operation they did in Voksh or were they stationed in Voksh?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know exactly because I was not in the command of that unit, but they operated there because they wanted to secure the canal, as they wanted to get weapons there, up till the end of the offensive when Junik --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you said, "For a while, they were," what time do you have in mind? A day? Two hours? A week?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It depended, it depended on the situation. Maybe they stayed for a week or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just be clear, both at page 85, line 11, and at page 85, line 18, the word appears which I think may either be a misunderstanding or a mistranslation, and may I just clarify that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You've just told us a few moments ago, that when they were in the areas around Voksh --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, if you want to clarify that they were securing a route through which a canal -- of course a channel could be -- that's how we understood it. Yes, if you want to clarify that, it's clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Just to be clear, the areas that you are speaking about are on the west side of the main road from Peje to Gjakove, those are the routes you're talking about. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Sllup, Drenoc, Voksh, Junik, that was the route --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, and --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that was followed by part of the population to go to Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And the job of the Black Eagles was, in part, to keep those routes of supply open on the west side of the road?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the purpose, because they fought with the Serbian forces at the time and the unit also have -- has now martyrs, you know, people who died, laid down their lives while fighting with the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And just so that we're clear, at pages 113 and 116 of your interview transcript, you describe the Black Eagles as being in movement, they were moving. What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on the situation. They were in the places that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And for a time --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how that could be interpreted, but that's a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And were they for a time located at Prilep and at Carrabreg at different times?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me about the subversive unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe they did go to assist during the offensive, but I don't know. But that would be normal for them to take part in fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Can I just ask you briefly about one aspect of the dates that you've given evidence about. You described an incident when a man called Besim came to make a complaint to you about the fact that he had been forced to dig trenches. And in your evidence, you said that took place in June. Is that your recollection?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in June, that's what I remember. I did not say that he was forced. He accepted to go and help.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Very well. In your witness statement, your consolidated witness statement at paragraph 49, you say that that incident occurred when Besim came to see you, "Sometime in May"; that is, not in June but in May. Do you know now whether it was May or June?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be exact with dates. When I was asked by the investigators of the Tribunal, I told them that I'm not prepared to give very exact dates, I'm not sure about dates, and that statement was given two years ago. I was allowed to carry on with the conversation with them, with the investigators, without being able to give exact dates, but it's been nine years, you know. But the event is what happened. I have described the event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I'm looking at the clock and I --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm reaching my conclusion now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, in your witness statement -- I'm sorry, in your interview at page 128, when you were describing this incident, you said that by the time of that complaint being made, the Black Eagles had a headquarters at Irzniq. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. They did not have a base at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, are you ready to cross-examine the witness? Mr. Cekaj, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Guy-Smith, who's counsel for Mr. Balaj. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, I want to spend a moment with you once again on the issue of dates, and I'd like you to listen very closely to my questions and I'm going to try to do this as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, if you want to establish positively a date, that's fine, but otherwise, let me just --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's what I'm going to be doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if you -- you want to establish, then please keep two things in mind: First, that dates may be right, may be wrong, those we talked about already, but the same might be true for things -- dates still to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You arrived in Irzniq as a commander on, I believe, the 26th of May; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said earlier, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before you arrived in Irzniq on the 26th of May, I suggest to you that the Black Eagles had just been formed as a result of a call for volunteers on May 14th in Irzniq. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that all of them were volunteers, but I don't know about the rest of the things you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I suggest to you that the Black Eagles did not exist as a unit at any time in April. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of what I personally heard, they had started at the time. They were part of the KLA after that, but I don't have any concrete or exact information beyond what I just said. Later on, I know that they were part of the -- of this unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say later on, you know they were part of this unit, you were aware of the fact that certainly by the time that you arrived in Irzniq, the Black Eagles had a specific function, and that's the function that you have described to us as a guerilla unit; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was informed about this by the staff, but very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Their function as a guerilla unit were to operate in the areas that you've just described to Mr. Emmerson among others, and by that I mean Voksh, Drenoc, Prilep; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say guerilla units, that's how they act. They have a mission, and after they carry out that mission they return to their base. But sometimes, according to the situation, they stayed to a certain -- in a certain part. But as far as I know, they moved around.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And, in fact, they stayed in Voksh for quite some time because there was a considerable engagement in Voksh between the KLA and Serbian forces regarding trying to keep that particular supply area open which the Serbs were trying to close down; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, I already said that once.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That occurred after you came to Irzniq and were the commander of subzone 2; right?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before you came to subzone -- the area that you've described as subzone 2, are you aware of the battles that occurred in Baballoq?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know who was the leader of the village of Baballoq during the battles before you arrived in Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of an individual by the name of Faik Dodaj as being the commander of the village of Baballoq?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Faik Dodaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And do you know him to be the commander of that area?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was responsible for a village. At that time I did not know him, but now I know him. It could be that he was a commander of a village.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He was also the commander of Shaptej, was he not?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the time that you were the commander in the village of Irzniq, you never saw the Black Eagles training, did you?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the time that you were the commander in the village of Irzniq, you had in your village five young men who operated as military police, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't have any specific training, but they were appointed to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Five of them; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: They wore black uniforms, did they not?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. They didn't have black uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the time that you spent talking to Besim, Besim told you that he met Toger and discussed working with him the day before they actually went together to go work; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On the day they went, they discussed - at least this is what he told me - they had discussed on that very day that they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You've told us that you spoke with Toger about Besim's upset and concerns; right?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He apologised to you; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You told him that he had operated outside of his sphere of influence, that that was something you should have been able to do, it was your village; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that any orders concerning the digging of trenches or any other kind of defensive formations was your responsibility and not others; right?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the responsibility of the village staff. I was responsible for those villages, but there was another person who was a commander of the village, as I mentioned earlier. But when it came to asking assistance -- when it came to someone asking for assistance from outside the village, he had to contact the village commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that was part of what your concern was because the Black Eagles unit and Toger were people who were from outside of the village; right?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Adem Hulaj, how old a man was he?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He must -- now he must be in his 60s.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you learned of this incident, you had no information about what the confrontation or the discussion between Adem Hulaj and Togeri was, did you?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't have information.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You have no idea what happened before Adem Hulaj was shot, do you?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no other information, apart from what I stated in my statement because I wasn't present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you talked to your niece, what you learned from your niece, which is what you said in your statement, was that immediately after the incident, Toger was holding his head saying something like, Why did I do this; right?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe he felt sad at what he had done. This is my personal assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Based on the information that you received from your -- from your niece --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- it was clear to you from the information that she gave you that this was an accident; true?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how she explained it to me, in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Adem -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You may go --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Adem Hulaj was a -- a friend of Ramush's father, Hilmi, was he not?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you learn that there was a discussion between Hilmi and Adem Hulaj concerning this unfortunate accident and all the -- and the whole matter was resolved?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information about that. I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I have but a second to mark off things, I will go even quicker.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The reason that you went to visit the woman in the village of --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I don't know if we need to go into private session for purposes of mentioning the village or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps -- perhaps it's wiser to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say that you -- you went for the purpose of -- of humanitarian purposes and for no other purposes, part of your concern was that this was a situation where there was a woman living by herself with some children; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was living outside the village, and I went to visit her, as I said, for humanitarian purposes to ask her whether she had some problems, some concerns.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you visited her, she told you that the family was disturbed by people who she didn't know and that they were civilians; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the evening hours. I don't know how -- if she was sincere in what she said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Whether or not she was sincere in what she said, that was the information she gave you, that people were --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did she tell you that she didn't know who these people were?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And she told you, did she not, that they would introduce themselves being from different villages?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't discuss this. It was a very brief talk, actually. I didn't stay there long. It was not part of my responsibility; it was part of the village responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Based on the conversation that you had with her, were you satisfied that the -- the village commander, Sokol Halilaj, was in a position to take care of any further concerns that she might have?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: One --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Richard, I'm getting there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: One last thing, sir. The gentleman you spoke to, Besim, Besim had, if I'm not mistaken, been involved in helping transport arms back from Albania, had he not?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He went with the village people. That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When he went with the village people, the reason that he went was to collect weapons to bring back to the village to defend the village; right?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is -- that was the main purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He was what would be called an Egyptian; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He speaks Albanian. It's his own problem how he -- what nationality or ethnicity he belongs to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That I appreciate. What I'm getting at is that he was -- he was considered to be Roma or Egyptian, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how they are called, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And he was interested, like everybody else in the village, in helping defend the village against the Serbian attacks; right?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Cekaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Harvey, who's counsel for Mr. Brahimaj. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm counsel for Mr. Brahimaj. I have about five questions to ask you. You and I have got five minutes in order to finish up today; right? Okay?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So I'm going to try and keep it short, and if possible if you can answer yes or no, then that will get us -- that will get you out of that chair before the end of the day. Okay? First question: You said in answer to Mr. Emmerson just now that the attack on Jablanica in August, you thought was on the 8th of August; in fact, I'm going to suggest to you, it was the 2nd and 3rd of August. Is it right that you might be mistaken when you said the 8th?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I might be mistaken. It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Secondly, in your witness statement at paragraph 41, for those who wish to follow, you said that - and I'm going to quote from your statement: "The KLA inside Kosovo wanted to have the KLA General Staff inside Kosovo." Is it correct that for those of you who were operating inside Kosovo, and we're talking in the month of July 1998, there was a concern that you needed to have the General Staff inside Kosovo and not outside?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is rather unclear --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: If it's --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can ask it in a better way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: In July of 1998, was there a feeling that the General Staff was remote and outside of Kosovo, and they need to be here with us?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indiscernible] unclear. The -- there was a demand for the KLA staff to be inside Kosova and not outside it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And I think you -- I'm sorry. I think you've said elsewhere that for you at that time, it was very unclear who the General Staff were and where they were, for you?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not that it was unclear, but we didn't know where it was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I'm going to turn -- turning to paragraph 47 of your statement, three lines from the bottom, you used this expression -- or five lines up: "On the 12th of August in the afternoon, the Serb forces returned to the same villages they had been through the day before with the looting units," and you use that term "looting units." Was it your impression or your information that the Serbs had special units whose job it was to loot, burn, and destroy villages after they had initially been occupied by their troops?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you already said, I think that there were units on the 12th, on the 12th of August, which entered the villages with looting forces, as I said, along with military or paramilitary formations that they had. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And not just on the 12th of August, but on a significant number of occasions that happened to the villages that you --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In many occasions, but we are talking now about this particular one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to move to my final topic with you, and that concerns the meetings of officers with whom you worked on the -- in the Dukagjin plateau, the Dukagjin Plain. Is it right that you attended quite a lot of meetings, maybe just small ones, two or three sometimes, sometimes larger, but quite a lot of meetings of officers to coordinate your work during the months in the summer of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had all sorts of meetings in various places, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So usually about -- about once a week or more often than that?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once a week, twice a week, once in two weeks, it depended on the changing circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I now want to come to some specific words in your interview of which we have the transcript, and I'm going to page 73 for those who wish to follow specifically. And this relates to the time when there has been a meeting at which Lahi Brahimaj was present and he was elected deputy commander. You remember that meeting?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: 23rd or 24th June?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Right, 23rd of June. And you said on page 73 that: "We were informed that Lahi Brahimaj was not his deputy anymore, but Nazmi Brahimaj is," and you were asked who informed you, and you said: "Ramush." And that was about a week after that meeting on the 23rd. Will you just confirm that that's correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there are some mistakes there. Someone informed us, but after two weeks Lahi Brahimaj's position was changed in the General Staff, and he was replaced with his brother Nazmi Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Right. And you said - I'm looking at page 74 now - and you said after that, you didn't see Lahi Brahimaj anymore?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lahi Brahimaj went to the General Staff of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And finally this, at page 75, you said: "Later on, he introduced himself as office of finance manager in the General Staff. He didn't participate anymore in the meetings." You would agree with that? When I say "didn't participate anymore in the meetings," that's your meetings that you had as officers in Dukagjin area?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he was doing the job you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed, Mr. Cekaj.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Harvey. I have some difficulties in finding on page 75 exactly what you quoted he had said, especially the part: "He didn't participate anymore in the meetings."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: It's four lines up from the bottom: "Interpreter: I -- he didn't participate anymore in the meetings."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. Thank you very much. Mr. Kearney, you really have to focus on what is really essential.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I will. I have three very brief questions. While I'm asking the first one, perhaps we could -- we could pull up Exhibit 318.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, just in terms of the last question by Mr. Harvey, after the 23rd of June did you ever go to Jablanica again?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the 23rd of June, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I went.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I want to show you again for this map, 318. You were asked many, many questions about it during your cross-examination. I want to ask you simply: From your answers on cross-examination, is it true that from the latter part of April through May, June, July, August, and even into the very early part of September, the KLA could move freely within this entire zone except when there were Serb offences. Is that true, sir?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was. At wartime, with the exception of August and September -- excuse me, with the exception of month [as interpreted] and September, it could during the other months but always depending on the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And this August offensive we've been talking about, the dates we've mentioned --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just, I'm sorry to interrupt, but line 12, I'm sorry, something seems to have gone wrong with the answer there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: With the word "month."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just check it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "With the exception of" and then something needs clarification, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I lost my present -- one second, please. Yes. Could you ask the witness -- could you again say -- you said: "With the exception of the month," and then you mentioned a month and then "and September." What was the first month you mentioned as an exception to it being wartime?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the months that there were no Serb offensives. The KLA units or members who were not in positions could move around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, when we find --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because it was a war situation, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When we find such a sign, it will be checked overnight and so that it appears tomorrow in the definite version a better way. Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: This August offensive that we've been talking about, Mr. Cekaj, forgetting about the exact dates of it for a moment, but from the answers that you gave on cross-examination, is it true that the ground portion of that offensive lasted only two daytime periods, on two days that were successive. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It ended on the 12th, and there wasn't any other offensive until September, during which time the KLA units and the population returned, trying to restore normal life --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I want to follow-up again --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It must be something very urgent because Mr. Kearney has only three questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't think that's a fair summary of the witness's evidence. What he said was in the entry into those villages took place over two days not the ground offensive took place over two days. The witness's evidence is that there was an offensive taking place from either the 7th and the 8th until the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: That's exactly what I'm trying to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kearney, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, the August offensive, the ground portion, not the shelling, just the ground portion of it, is it true that the Serbs went into the villages in question on one day, withdrew before nightfall, and then went back the following day, and then withdrew again. Is that what happened, sir?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true that they entered in the direction of Baballoq, Gllogjan, Shaptej, up to Irzniq from the east. From the other side, Prilep, Carrabreg, in the south-western part, they entered up to Irzniq, accomplished their mission, as I said, and then they withdrew on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Lastly, you said that -- you were asked about the Black Eagles training. You said during your direct examination that they trained on a cooperative piece of land north-east of Gllogjan. I want to ask you how you know that. Who did you hear that from, sir?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there myself, but that was my guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you know personally members of the Black Eagles unit?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
