utterances.text: There were members from my village as well, whom I knew, along with others from the surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And did you talk to them about the activities of the Black Eagles unit itself?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had very little contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a few questions for you. I hope to go through it very quickly. In your village, was there anyone else with the name similar like yours, that is Shemsedin and then Cekaj or Ceku, or are you the only one who has this first name and family name?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't get translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll repeat the question. Do you hear me now? Yes.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear your question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will repeat it.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In your village, is there anyone else with a name similar like yours; that is, first name and family name, meaning someone by the name of Shemsedin and then Cekaj or Ceku?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to turn into private session for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One final question. When asked by Mr. Kearney about the -- where the Black Eagles trained, you said it was a guess that it was in the place you mentioned. Now, the guess was based on what?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because that is a suitable terrain for training soldiers, and as a soldier myself, I thought that that would be a good place to train KLA soldiers. That was my assumption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I've got no further questions. Have the questions of the Bench triggered any further questions? Then, Mr. Cekaj, this concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you for coming and for answering all the questions that have been put to you, both by the parties and by the Bench. And I hope that you have a safe trip home again. Madam Usher, could you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, the scheduling issues I have suggested to discuss them not in this courtroom, and therefore I would like first -- unless there's anything --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Just a minor housekeeping matter, Your Honour. I wanted to tender into evidence the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will do that next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, there's a lot of things to be said about that. The only thing is have the others still numbers to be assigned to documents because I would at least have them marked for identification, but I think we had them all, if I'm not wrong, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There are, in fact, one or two documents which next week I may seek to tender from the bar table because time ran out in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's a different matter. But no documents that have been used and which have not been assigned numbers marked for identification. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: That's my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Yes. Then I would like to thank especially the interpreters, the technicians, but also transcribers, but also security, I mean everyone who helped us to achieve that finally we could finish this witness and to make it possible that he would not have to stay over for a couple of days on the weekend just to answer the last couple of questions. Thank you very much. And it's also in view of your schedules, also your personal schedules, that we'll not continue in court with matters for which -- which might even be a bit boring. We adjourn until Monday, the 21st of May, quarter past 2.00, in Courtroom I, subject to the outcome of further conversations today on the scheduling. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 21st day of May, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
